title.es: Cómo se construye un segmento de pódcast

es: Reconocer marcadores del discurso oral (anyway, by the way, as I was saying, to sum up, before we go) y saber si abren, cambian de tema, resumen o cierran.

teaching.en: The host opens the segment with «welcome back to the show» and then, «to begin with», she sets out the topic of this episode.
teaching.es: La presentadora abre el segmento con «bienvenidos de nuevo al programa» y, «para empezar», expone el tema de este episodio.
teaching.explanationEs: Welcome back y to begin with abren el segmento y presentan el tema.
segments: The host opens the segment with «welcome back to the show» and
then, «to begin with», she sets out the topic of this episode.
teaching.audioText: The host opens the segment with «welcome back to the show» and then, «to begin with», she sets out the topic of this episode.

teaching.en: When a guest drifts onto a tangent, the host can say «anyway» or «moving on» to steer the conversation back to the main topic.
teaching.es: Cuando un invitado se va por la tangente, la presentadora puede decir «bueno» o «pasando a otra cosa» para reconducir la conversación al tema principal.
teaching.explanationEs: Anyway y moving on cierran una idea y abren otra; van al principio de la frase, con coma.
segments: When a guest drifts onto a tangent, the host can say «anyway»
or «moving on» to steer the conversation back to the main topic.
teaching.audioText: When a guest drifts onto a tangent, the host can say «anyway» or «moving on» to steer the conversation back to the main topic.

teaching.en: «By the way» is a marker for an aside: it lets a speaker add a side detail without abandoning the thread of the segment.
teaching.es: «Por cierto» es un marcador de inciso: permite añadir un detalle lateral sin abandonar el hilo del segmento.
teaching.explanationEs: By the way sale un momento del tema principal para dar un dato, pero no cambia de tema.
segments: «By the way» is a marker for an aside: it lets a
speaker add a side detail without abandoning the thread of the segment.
teaching.audioText: «By the way» is a marker for an aside: it lets a speaker add a side detail without abandoning the thread of the segment.

teaching.en: «As I was saying» picks up a thought that a guest had interrupted, so the listener can reconnect with the earlier point.
teaching.es: «Como iba diciendo» retoma una idea que un invitado había interrumpido, para que el oyente conecte de nuevo con el punto anterior.
teaching.explanationEs: As I was saying = como iba diciendo: retoma una idea que quedó cortada.
segments: «As I was saying» picks up a thought that a guest
had interrupted, so the listener can reconnect with the earlier point.
teaching.audioText: «As I was saying» picks up a thought that a guest had interrupted, so the listener can reconnect with the earlier point.

teaching.en: «To sum up» and «in short» signal that the host is about to condense the whole episode into one closing idea.
teaching.es: «En resumen» y «en pocas palabras» indican que la presentadora va a condensar todo el episodio en una idea final.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up y in short anuncian el resumen; so también puede abrir una conclusión.
segments: «To sum up» and «in short» signal that the host is
about to condense the whole episode into one closing idea.
teaching.audioText: «To sum up» and «in short» signal that the host is about to condense the whole episode into one closing idea.

teaching.en: «Before we go» announces the ending of the segment, so it usually comes just ahead of a thank-you or a preview of the next episode.
teaching.es: «Antes de despedirnos» anuncia el final del segmento, así que suele ir justo antes de un agradecimiento o un avance del próximo episodio.
teaching.explanationEs: Before we go y that is all for today cierran el segmento.
segments: «Before we go» announces the ending of the segment, so it usually comes
just ahead of a thank-you or a preview of the next episode.
teaching.audioText: «Before we go» announces the ending of the segment, so it usually comes just ahead of a thank-you or a preview of the next episode.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función tiene «anyway» en esta intervención de la presentadora?

choices.text: It adds a side detail without leaving the main topic.
It picks up a point the guest had interrupted.
It politely ends the side story and moves on.

feedback.es: Anyway cierra la anécdota del invitado con cortesía y pasa a la siguiente pregunta: cambia de tema.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que dice la presentadora justo después del marcador.

origin.text: The guest has just spent five minutes describing his holiday. The host smiles politely and says: «Anyway, let us move on to the next question about screens.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Por cierto, nuestro invitado acaba de publicar un libro sobre el sueño.»

answer.text: By

feedback.es: By the way introduce un dato extra fuera del hilo principal; el segmento volverá después a ese libro.

hint.es: Es la preposición que también traduce «por» en «por cierto».

origin.text: ___ the way, our guest has just published a book on sleep, and we will come back to it after the break.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Eso es todo por hoy, así que gracias por escuchar.»

answer.text: That is all for today, so thank you for listening

feedback.es: That is all for today es un marcador de cierre y va seguido de la frase de agradecimiento al oyente.

hint.es: Primero el marcador de cierre; al final, la frase que agradece.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del programa con la función que cumple.

pairs: Welcome back, and to begin with, a quick word on tonight's topic.
Moving on, let us look at how screens affect teenagers.
In short, a steady routine matters more than total hours.
Thank you for listening, and see you next week.

feedback.es: Cada marcador cumple una función en el segmento: abrir, cambiar de tema, resumir o cerrar.

pairs: Welcome back, and to begin with, a quick word on tonight's topic.
Moving on, let us look at how screens affect teenagers.
In short, a steady routine matters more than total hours.
Thank you for listening, and see you next week.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué fin usa Tom «as I was saying» en su pódcast?

choices.text: To return to his main point after the story.
To add a side comment about his cousin's exams.
To change to a topic different from the story.

feedback.es: As I was saying retoma la idea principal que la historia de su primo había dejado a medias.

origin.text: Tom is recording a podcast about study habits. After a long story about his cousin's exams, he pauses and says: as I was saying, the key is not how long you study but how often you review.

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés: «Bueno, pasemos a la siguiente pregunta sobre el sueño.»

answer.text: Anyway, let us move on to the next question about sleep.
accepted: Anyway, let us move on to the next question about sleep.
Anyway, let's move on to the next question about sleep.
Moving on, let us turn to the next question about sleep.

feedback.es: Anyway o moving on abren la frase con coma y no llevan but: el cambio de tema ya está marcado.

origin.text: Quieres pasar a la siguiente pregunta después de una anécdota larga del invitado.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y elige qué da a entender la presentadora con «anyway».

choices.text: That she finds the story useless and wants the guest to stop speaking.
That she enjoyed the story but wants the segment back on its topic.
That the story was relevant and she wants him to develop it further.

feedback.es: Elogia la historia («a great story») pero exige volver al sueño: reconoce el valor de la anécdota y reconduce el tema.

origin.audio: Halfway through the episode, the host lets her guest talk about his first marathon for almost ten minutes. Finally she smiles and says: anyway, that is a great story, but let us get back to sleep, which is the topic of today's segment. The guest laughs and apologises for going off on a tangent. By the way, he adds, I slept badly for a whole week before the race, and that is exactly the point I wanted to make.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué el invitado añade «by the way».

choices.text: To carry on with the marathon story, ignoring the host's request.
To claim that the host had not understood his story.
To link his marathon story to the sleep topic with a fresh detail.

feedback.es: Su inciso aporta un dato (durmió mal una semana) que conecta la anécdota con el tema central del segmento.

origin.audio: Halfway through the episode, the host lets her guest talk about his first marathon for almost ten minutes. Finally she smiles and says: anyway, that is a great story, but let us get back to sleep, which is the topic of today's segment. The guest laughs and apologises for going off on a tangent. By the way, he adds, I slept badly for a whole week before the race, and that is exactly the point I wanted to make.

prompt.es: Completa: «Perdona, me fui por la tangente.»

answer.text: tangent

feedback.es: Go off on a tangent es la colocación para desviarse del tema; el hablante lo reconoce y vuelve al punto principal.

origin.text: I am sorry, I went off on a ___ there. Let me bring it back to the main point of the segment.

prompt.es: Cierra tu segmento: despedida, resumen y aviso del próximo episodio.

answer.text: Before we go, let me sum up the main idea of today's segment: good sleep habits improve everything else. Next week's episode is about stress, so please join us again.
accepted: Before we go, let me sum up the main idea of today's segment: good sleep habits improve everything else. Next week's episode is about stress, so please join us again.
That is all for today. To sum up, the main idea is that good sleep habits improve everything else. Our next episode is about stress, so see you then.
Before we go, in short: good habits improve everything else. See you next week, because the next episode is about stress.

feedback.es: Un buen cierre combina un marcador de despedida, otro de resumen con la idea principal y un aviso del siguiente episodio.

origin.text: Cierra tu segmento sobre el sueño: usa un marcador de cierre, un marcador de resumen con la idea principal (los buenos hábitos mejoran todo lo demás) y avisa de que el próximo episodio trata del estrés.

prompt.es: Lee la nota de la editora. ¿Qué le sugiere a la presentadora?

choices.text: To bring the guest back earlier, while still allowing brief asides.
To avoid every aside so that the guest never leaves the topic.
To wait even longer before using a marker that changes the topic.

feedback.es: Acepta los incisos breves (a short by the way is fine) pero pide reconducir antes las historias largas.

origin.text: Note from the editor: The opening worked well, but when the guest drifted off the topic with a story about his marathon, you waited five minutes before saying anyway. Next time, steer him back sooner; a short by the way is fine, a long story is not.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como iba diciendo, el verdadero problema no es el celular en sí.»

answer.text: As I was saying, the real problem is not the phone itself

feedback.es: As I was saying retoma la idea interrumpida y la frase sigue con el orden normal: sujeto, verbo y complemento.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes de despedirnos, quiero agradecer a nuestro invitado.»

answer.text: Before

feedback.es: Before we go anuncia el final del episodio y prepara los agradecimientos de la presentadora.

origin.text: The interview ran long, so the host glanced at the clock and said: «___ we go, let me thank our guest.» Then the closing music began.

es: Parafrasear y resumir lo que dice otra persona con verbos de habla (claim, point out, admit, suggest, deny, refuse, promise, warn) y su patrón.

teaching.en: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is excessive, yet the authors of the study maintain that most adults need it.
teaching.es: Algunos expertos afirman que ocho horas de sueño son excesivas, pero los autores del estudio sostienen que la mayoría de los adultos las necesita.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim that deja la duda sobre lo dicho; maintain that sostiene una postura pese a la oposición.
segments: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is excessive, yet
the authors of the study maintain that most adults need it.
teaching.audioText: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is excessive, yet the authors of the study maintain that most adults need it.

teaching.en: In the summary, critics point out that the sample was small, so the authors refuse to draw firm conclusions from it.
teaching.es: En el resumen, los críticos señalan que la muestra era pequeña, por lo que los autores se niegan a sacar conclusiones firmes.
teaching.explanationEs: Point out that + oración introduce un dato; refuse va seguido de to + verbo.
segments: In the summary, critics point out that the sample was small,
so the authors refuse to draw firm conclusions from it.
teaching.audioText: In the summary, critics point out that the sample was small, so the authors refuse to draw firm conclusions from it.

teaching.en: The minister was forced to acknowledge that the plan had failed, although she tried to downplay the scale of the losses.
teaching.es: La ministra se vio obligada a reconocer que el plan había fracasado, aunque intentó quitar importancia a la magnitud de las pérdidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Acknowledge that reconoce un hecho incómodo; downplay + nombre resta importancia.
segments: The minister was forced to acknowledge that the plan had failed,
although she tried to downplay the scale of the losses.
teaching.audioText: The minister was forced to acknowledge that the plan had failed, although she tried to downplay the scale of the losses.

teaching.en: Many users admit checking their phones at night, but some flatly deny doing it, even when the screen-time data says otherwise.
teaching.es: Muchos usuarios admiten mirar el celular por la noche, pero algunos lo niegan rotundamente, incluso cuando los datos de uso dicen lo contrario.
teaching.explanationEs: Admit y deny se construyen con -ing cuando hablan de la propia acción del sujeto; flatly refuerza la negación.
segments: Many users admit checking their phones at night, but some flatly
deny doing it, even when the screen-time data says otherwise.
teaching.audioText: Many users admit checking their phones at night, but some flatly deny doing it, even when the screen-time data says otherwise.

teaching.en: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn people against drinking coffee late in the evening.
teaching.es: Los médicos sugieren acostarse más temprano y advierten a la gente contra el café por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + -ing (nunca to + verbo); warn against + -ing advierte de un riesgo.
segments: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn
people against drinking coffee late in the evening.
teaching.audioText: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn people against drinking coffee late in the evening.

teaching.en: Some guests promise to reply later, but the host will not summarise the debate until every claim has been checked.
teaching.es: Algunos invitados prometen responder más tarde, pero la presentadora no resumirá el debate hasta que se compruebe cada afirmación.
teaching.explanationEs: Promise va seguido de to + verbo; en un resumen cada verbo de habla debe respetar lo que se dijo.
segments: Some guests promise to reply later, but the host will
not summarise the debate until every claim has been checked.
teaching.audioText: Some guests promise to reply later, but the host will not summarise the debate until every claim has been checked.

prompt.es: Elige el informe que respeta la actitud del ingeniero en esta entrevista.

choices.text: The engineer admitted that there had been a fault.
The engineer claimed that there had been a fault.
The engineer denied that there had been a fault.

feedback.es: Reconoce un fallo que le incomoda («we did not notice it»): admit transmite esa actitud, claim la pondría en duda.

hint.es: Piensa si el ingeniero defiende algo discutible o reconoce algo incómodo.

origin.text: Interviewer: Was the bridge closed because of a fault? Engineer: Yes, there was a fault, and we did not notice it soon enough.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los docentes sugieren empezar más tarde y advierten contra madrugar.»

answer.text: suggest

feedback.es: Suggest admite el patrón -ing (suggest starting); no podría seguir con to + verbo.

hint.es: El verbo va seguido de starting: busca el que admite -ing y significa «proponer».

origin.text: Teachers ___ starting later, and they warn against getting up too early.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El gerente admitió haber cometido un grave error el año pasado.»

answer.text: The manager admitted making a serious mistake last year

feedback.es: Admit se construye con -ing cuando el sujeto habla de algo que él mismo hizo.

hint.es: Después del verbo de habla va el gerundio: making.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los investigadores, sin embargo, sostienen que hacen falta más pruebas.»

answer.text: maintain

feedback.es: Maintain that refleja que los investigadores sostienen su postura frente a lo que afirma el folleto.

origin.text: The company's leaflet claims that the drink is safe. Other researchers, however, ___ that more tests are needed before anyone can say so.

prompt.es: ¿Qué informe recoge fielmente lo que dijo el entrenador tras el partido?

choices.text: The coach admitted that the team had played badly and promised to change it.
The coach admitted that the team had played badly and refused to change it.
The coach claimed that the team had played badly and denied making excuses.

feedback.es: Reconoce que jugaron mal y se niega a cambiar el equipo: los otros informes invierten o deforman una de las dos ideas.

origin.text: Coach: «I will be honest with you: we played badly. I will not make excuses, and I will not change the team on Saturday.»

prompt.es: Cuenta con un verbo de habla lo que dijo el médico.

answer.text: The doctor warned us not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
accepted: The doctor warned us not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
The doctor warned us not to drink coffee after six.
The doctor warned people not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
The doctor warned against drinking coffee after six o'clock.
The doctor warned against drinking coffee after six.
The doctor warned me not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
The doctor warned you not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
The doctor advised us not to drink coffee after six o'clock.

feedback.es: Warn + persona + not to + verbo transmite una advertencia; el médico no se limita a decir algo: avisa de un riesgo.

origin.text: Doctor: «Do not drink coffee after six o'clock: it is bad for your sleep.»

prompt.es: Escucha el debate y elige el resumen más fiel de la postura de la directora.

choices.text: She accepts there are problems and agrees to review the change after a month.
She ignores every complaint and will not publish the cost figures.
She accepts there are problems but will not cancel the change yet.

feedback.es: Reconoce que el horario no es perfecto, pero se niega a cancelarlo antes de tener resultados de un año completo.

origin.audio: At the end of the radio debate, the head of the school defends the new timetable. It is not perfect, she admits, and lessons now start earlier than many families would like. Even so, she maintains that students concentrate better in the morning, and she refuses to cancel the change before a full year of results is available. Asked about the cost of the extra buses, she promises to publish every figure next month, but she downplays the complaints from parents.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender al negarse a cancelar el cambio ahora.

choices.text: That she wants a full year of evidence before deciding about the change.
That she has already decided the change works and ignores the evidence.
That she accepts the parents' complaints but has no power to act.

feedback.es: Condiciona la decisión a un año completo de resultados: pide pruebas antes de juzgar, no anticipa ni el fracaso ni el éxito.

origin.audio: At the end of the radio debate, the head of the school defends the new timetable. It is not perfect, she admits, and lessons now start earlier than many families would like. Even so, she maintains that students concentrate better in the morning, and she refuses to cancel the change before a full year of results is available. Asked about the cost of the extra buses, she promises to publish every figure next month, but she downplays the complaints from parents.

prompt.es: Completa: «El gerente se negó a comentar hasta que se publicaran los resultados.»

answer.text: refused

feedback.es: Refuse to + verbo expresa una negativa directa; promise to + verbo, en cambio, compromete a hacer algo después.

origin.text: Asked about the missing money, the manager ___ to comment until the results were published, although he promised to reply later.

prompt.es: Cuenta con tres verbos de habla lo que dice una compañera en su nota.

answer.text: My colleague admits making a mistake in the third table, warns that the figures may be wrong, and promises to send a corrected version on Monday.
accepted: My colleague admits making a mistake in the third table, warns that the figures may be wrong, and promises to send a corrected version on Monday.
My colleague admitted making a mistake in the third table, warned us that the figures might be wrong and promised to send a corrected version on Monday.
My colleague acknowledges that he made a mistake in the third table, warns that the figures may be wrong, and promises to send a corrected version on Monday.

feedback.es: El resumen fiel convierte cada idea en un verbo de habla con su patrón: admit + -ing, warn + that, promise + to.

origin.text: Note from a colleague: «I made a mistake in the third table. The figures may be wrong. Please do not share the report before Friday, and I will send a corrected version on Monday.»

evidenceGroups: admits that he made a mistake
admitted that he made a mistake
admits that she made a mistake
admitted that she made a mistake
acknowledges that he made a mistake
acknowledged that he made a mistake
acknowledges that she made a mistake
acknowledged that she made a mistake

prompt.es: Lee el comunicado del ayuntamiento. ¿Qué resumen es fiel?

choices.text: The council promises that the bridge will reopen in June and apologises for the delay.
The council regrets the delay and acknowledges that June is not certain.
The council admits the delay was its fault and advises residents to avoid the old route.

feedback.es: El comunicado lamenta el retraso y deja la fecha de junio abierta a nuevos problemas: no promete ni niega nada.

origin.text: Council statement: «We regret the delay. The bridge will reopen in June, although we cannot rule out further problems. Residents who use the old route should plan for extra time.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Varios expertos señalan que la encuesta fue demasiado corta.»

answer.text: Several experts point out that the survey was far too short

feedback.es: Point out + that introduce el dato que el hablante señala; la oración subordinada mantiene el orden sujeto + verbo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud transmite la directora en esta respuesta a un periodista?

choices.text: She accepts the company knew but insists it acted as fast as possible.
She blames the supplier alone and refuses to accept any fault.
She concedes that the company was slow but shares the blame.

feedback.es: Acepta su parte del error («we should have acted sooner»), pero añade que el proveedor tampoco ayudó: reconoce sin cargar toda la culpa.

origin.text: Journalist: Did the company know about the fault? Director: We found out about it in March, and I accept that we should have acted sooner, although the supplier did not help either.

title.en: Take notes from a health segment
title.es: Tomar notas de un segmento de salud

es: Tomar notas de un segmento de audio sobre salud separando la idea principal, los detalles, los ejemplos y la recomendación.

teaching.en: Before you jot down anything, listen for the gist: the main idea usually appears in the first sentences or in the final summary.
teaching.es: Antes de apuntar nada, escucha la idea general: la idea principal suele aparecer en las primeras frases o en el resumen final.
teaching.explanationEs: El gist es la esencia del mensaje; jot down = apuntar rápido, con pocas palabras.
segments: Before you jot down anything, listen for the gist: the main idea
usually appears in the first sentences or in the final summary.
teaching.audioText: Before you jot down anything, listen for the gist: the main idea usually appears in the first sentences or in the final summary.

teaching.en: A detail supports the main idea with research, figures or an example, for instance a study of a short nap after lunch, and it often follows markers such as first or also.
teaching.es: Un detalle apoya la idea principal con investigación, cifras o un ejemplo, por ejemplo un estudio sobre una siesta corta tras comer, y suele ir tras marcadores como first o also.
teaching.explanationEs: El detalle no es el mensaje central: lo demuestra, lo mide o lo ilustra.
segments: A detail supports the main idea with research, figures or an example, for instance a study
of a short nap after lunch, and it often follows markers such as first or also.
teaching.audioText: A detail supports the main idea with research, figures or an example, for instance a study of a short nap after lunch, and it often follows markers such as first or also.

teaching.en: Jot down keywords rather than whole sentences: a good note is short enough to read at a glance but complete enough to rebuild the idea later.
teaching.es: Apunta palabras clave en lugar de frases enteras: una buena nota es lo bastante corta para leerla de un vistazo y lo bastante completa para reconstruir la idea después.
teaching.explanationEs: Note = nota; escribe palabras clave, cifras y nombres, no la frase completa.
segments: Jot down keywords rather than whole sentences: a good note is short enough
to read at a glance but complete enough to rebuild the idea later.
teaching.audioText: Jot down keywords rather than whole sentences: a good note is short enough to read at a glance but complete enough to rebuild the idea later.

teaching.en: The speaker adds a caveat whenever the evidence has limits, for example when a study followed only a small group of volunteers.
teaching.es: El locutor añade una salvedad siempre que las pruebas tienen límites, por ejemplo cuando un estudio siguió solo a un grupo pequeño de voluntarios.
teaching.explanationEs: Una caveat limita hasta dónde vale la evidencia; suele ir tras but, however o even so.
segments: The speaker adds a caveat whenever the evidence has limits, for
example when a study followed only a small group of volunteers.
teaching.audioText: The speaker adds a caveat whenever the evidence has limits, for example when a study followed only a small group of volunteers.

teaching.en: The benefit of caffeine is sharper concentration during the day, whereas the risk is a chronic lack of sleep if you drink it too late.
teaching.es: El beneficio de la cafeína es una concentración más aguda durante el día, mientras que el riesgo es una falta crónica de sueño si se toma demasiado tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Benefit y risk son detalles de signo opuesto: lo que se gana y lo que se arriesga.
segments: The benefit of caffeine is sharper concentration during the day, whereas the risk
is a chronic lack of sleep if you drink it too late.
teaching.audioText: The benefit of caffeine is sharper concentration during the day, whereas the risk is a chronic lack of sleep if you drink it too late.

teaching.en: The speaker's recommendation closes the segment: put the phone away an hour before bed, so that your body can wind down.
teaching.es: La recomendación del locutor cierra el segmento: guarda el celular una hora antes de dormir, para que tu cuerpo se relaje.
teaching.explanationEs: La recomendación es lo que el locutor te pide hacer; casi siempre va al final. Wind down = relajarse.
segments: The speaker's recommendation closes the segment: put the phone away an
hour before bed, so that your body can wind down.
teaching.audioText: The speaker's recommendation closes the segment: put the phone away an hour before bed, so that your body can wind down.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la idea principal que anotarías del inicio del segmento.

choices.text: Teenagers sleep an hour less than adults because school starts so early.
Late phone use cuts teenagers' sleep and can harm their mood and memory.
Phones help teenagers relax, so they sleep an hour longer than before.

feedback.es: La presentadora enlaza el uso del celular con menos sueño y con efectos en el ánimo y la memoria: es el mensaje central.

hint.es: Busca la frase que resume tanto la causa como la consecuencia.

origin.audio: Teenagers who use their phones until midnight usually sleep an hour less than those who switch off at ten. That is why the presenter begins with a warning: poor sleep is not a small problem, because it affects mood and memory.

prompt.es: Completa: «Apunta rápido la cifra clave y la recomendación.»

prompt.es: Escribe el resumen del segmento: tres verbos de habla y la postura de cada hablante.

answer.text: In this segment, the host and Dr Patel debate whether schools should record every lesson. Dr Patel is in favour: she maintains that recordings help students who miss a class or need to watch a difficult explanation again. She acknowledges that attendance may fall, but she insists that learning matters more than attendance. The host, by contrast, is sceptical. He fears that students will stop coming to school, and he points out that teachers feel watched. Dr Patel accepts that this is a fair concern, so she suggests recording only the main lessons and letting teachers remove private comments. The host calls this a reasonable compromise. Overall, the guest sounds confident, whereas the host remains cautious, but both want to protect learning.
accepted: In this segment, the host and Dr Patel debate whether schools should record every lesson. Dr Patel is in favour: she maintains that recordings help students who miss a class or need to watch a difficult explanation again. She acknowledges that attendance may fall, but she insists that learning matters more than attendance. The host, by contrast, is sceptical. He fears that students will stop coming to school, and he points out that teachers feel watched. Dr Patel accepts that this is a fair concern, so she suggests recording only the main lessons and letting teachers remove private comments. The host calls this a reasonable compromise. Overall, the guest sounds confident, whereas the host remains cautious, but both want to protect learning.

The segment is a debate between a host and Dr Patel about whether schools should record every lesson. According to the guest, recordings are useful for students who miss a class, and she argues that learning is more important than attendance. She admits that attendance could fall and accepts that teachers may feel watched, so she proposes recording only the main lessons. The host is sceptical because he worries that students will stop coming to school. He claims that a fully online model is risky, but he still calls her idea a reasonable compromise. To sum up, the guest is confident and practical, whereas the host is more cautious, although both speakers care about good learning.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen presenta el tema, atribuye las ideas con verbos variados, marca la postura de cada uno y cierra con una valoración global.

origin.text:
Host: Today we ask whether schools should record every lesson. Dr Patel, you are in favour.
Guest: I am. Recordings help students who miss a class, and they can watch a difficult explanation again. I acknowledge that attendance may fall, but I maintain that learning matters more than attendance.
Host: I am sceptical. If everything is online, will students still come? Also, teachers say they feel watched.
Guest: That is a fair concern, which is why I suggest recording only the main lessons and letting teachers remove private comments.
Host: That is a reasonable compromise. Before we go, thank you, Dr Patel.
